solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perhaps grey fake caught out by furniture specialist for us

indicators.note: something put out is ejected, so the named letter leaves the word

parts.note: a quack is a fake doctor
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Ercol is a British furniture maker
something for us is ours, so OUR

explanation.surface: A fake grey antique has been exposed by a furniture expert working on our behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: Ercol is a well-known British furniture company, founded in High Wycombe. Grey is offered only as an example, hence 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaker colour is the sober drab grey traditionally worn by Friends, so grey is one example of it.

clue.text: Question … one to check for somebody

parts.note: qu. is a standard abbreviation for question
the Roman numeral for one
to dam a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: Someone is being questioned and has to be checked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis is only decoration; the three pieces run straight on.
explanation.definitionFit: Quidam is Latin for 'a certain person', used in English for an unnamed individual or nobody in particular.

clue.text: Forbidding Scottish muscle with almost power of two

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is left off

parts.note: an ab is an abdominal muscle
two cubed is eight, a power of two

explanation.surface: A stern Scot flexes a muscle while doing a sum about powers of two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power of two' looks like strength times two; it is the mathematical sense, a number such as 2, 4 or 8.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots word means aloof or keeping at a distance, which matches a forbidding, standoffish manner.

clue.text: Vulgar old lump in Shrek?

indicators.note: to lump things together is to throw them in a heap, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written: the film ogre's name

explanation.surface: The ogre Shrek is coarse, an uncouth lump of a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lump' looks like a noun for the ogre's bulk, but it is the verb, heaping letters together. A kern was a lowly Irish foot soldier, hence a boor; the word is obsolete, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means boorish, like a kern or lout, which is the obsolete sense of coarse and vulgar.

clue.text: Shakespearean attempt at riddle recalled time involving Mark

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read back to front
to involve is to wrap up within, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: an age is a period of time
M abbreviates mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone tries to set a Shakespearean riddle about a time involving a man named Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: In Love's Labour's Lost the clown Costard says this for 'enigma', so it is a botched attempt at the word for riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Costard's garbled 'egma' is his mangled try at saying enigma, the learned word for a puzzle or conundrum.

clue.text: Scottish upset about another cup thrashing

indicators.note: a thrashing beats something up, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish side is downcast over yet another heavy defeat in a cup competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the anagram signal, but it belongs with 'Scottish' in the definition; 'thrashing' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots idiom means to overturn or come to grief, literally to upset the crane or pot-hanger.

clue.text: Sordid gains tempt boxing clubs

indicators.note: to box something is to put it inside a box, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to lure is to tempt
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Ill-gotten money lures boxing clubs into shady deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing clubs' reads as sporting gyms, but boxing is the verb of enclosing and clubs is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy lucre is the stock phrase for money gained dishonourably, so the word means sordid gains.

clue.text: Japan previously making raid on base

indicators.note: base means debased or corrupted, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In earlier times Japan launched a raid on a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' looks like the country and evokes Pearl Harbor, but it is a verb: in 19th-century slang to japan a man was to ordain him, from the black clerical garb.
explanation.definitionFit: Old university slang used japan, after the black lacquer, for admitting someone into holy orders as a clergyman.

clue.text: What could be making us single?

definitions.text: What could be making us single?

indicators.note: making means fashioning, so the letters are worked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rueful question about why we are still unattached.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: rearranged, two words become the answer, and the answer is a plausible reason for staying unpartnered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unattractive is a wry candidate for whatever keeps a person without a partner, so the question describes it.

clue.text: Turkic Asian heading for Ukraine for example, twice

indicators.note: a heading is what stands at the top, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the country
z.B., zum Beispiel, is German for 'for example'
the second rendering of 'for example', this time the English e.g.

explanation.surface: A Central Asian person heads for Ukraine, mentioned twice as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example, twice' asks for two abbreviations of the phrase: the German z.B. and the English e.g.
explanation.definitionFit: An Uzbeg, a variant of Uzbek, belongs to a Turkic people of Central Asia.

clue.text: Cheese? Me, I'm confused with colours

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asked about cheese admits to being baffled by colours.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'Cheese?' sound like an offer; it is just the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coulommiers is a soft white-rinded French cheese from the Brie region, named after its home town.

clue.text: Hard to excavate around ancient town

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
to grub is to dig up

explanation.surface: Archaeologists find it tough to dig around an ancient settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard to excavate' reads as a difficulty; 'to' just links the two pieces before the whole is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A burgh is an old Scottish chartered town, a variant of borough with a long history.

clue.text: Chinese warehouses slashing 50 per cent off their tea succeeded

indicators.note: slashing half off cuts a word in two and throws away one half

parts.note: souchong is a Chinese tea, and 'their' refers back to the Chinese
S abbreviates succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Chinese warehouses slash prices on their tea by half and the sale works.
explanation.walkthrough: The front half of the eight-letter tea goes. A hong was a foreign trading house or warehouse in Canton.
explanation.definitionFit: Hongs were the warehouses and trading establishments of merchants in old Canton, so the plural fits.

clue.text: Monsieur fighting unarmed

indicators.note: things fighting are in turmoil and thrashing about, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman goes into a fight without a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting unarmed' sounds like a description of the Frenchman; 'fighting' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical term, from Latin inermis, describes plants without thorns or spines, i.e. defenceless.

clue.text: Massage hip after party

indicators.note: coming after means following, so the first-named piece is placed second

parts.note: a do is a party
hip means fashionable, i.e. in

explanation.surface: Someone needs a hip massage after a heavy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip' looks like the body part being massaged; it is the adjective for trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Massage is slang for roughing someone up, and the phrasal verb means to beat up or wear out.

clue.text: Transport to Paddington perhaps put out by downpour

indicators.note: out can mean out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a downpour is heavy rain

explanation.surface: Rail travel to Paddington is disrupted by a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as inconvenienced; 'out' alone rearranges the three letters. Paddington is a London terminus, and trains towards London are 'up' trains.
explanation.definitionFit: In British railway usage an up train is one travelling towards London, such as one into Paddington station.

clue.text: Byzantine grail that is pure clay

indicators.note: Byzantine means intricately tangled, so the letters are knotted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sacred Byzantine vessel turns out to be made of pure clay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Byzantine' looks like a description of the grail's origin; it is the convoluted sense that signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Argil is potter's clay, especially white clay, so it names clay in an unmixed state.

clue.text: Type of memory professor adopted by actually declining Latin

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so one piece is taken inside another
to decline is to refuse or turn away, so that letter is turned away from the word

parts.note: really means actually
L is the abbreviation for Latin
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A professor's memory is said to be fading, along with Latin teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Ls in the word for actually goes, and the don sits in the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Read-only memory, ROM, is computer storage that can be read but not written to, a kind of memory.

clue.text: English expressing extremes of skills in throwing and kicking

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other
to express is to press out, as juice from fruit, so those letters are squeezed out

parts.note: tossing is throwing

indicators.note: extremes are the two far ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English sportsman shows the full range of skills, from throwing to kicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremes of skills' gives two Ss, which are pressed out of the word for throwing, and E is put in where they were.
explanation.definitionFit: To toe a ball is to strike it with the toe of the boot, so toeing is a kind of kicking.

clue.text: Office keeping a Japanese coin back, a gold coin

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: the offices is an old euphemism for the lavatory, and a john is a lavatory
taken as written

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: the sen is a former Japanese coin, a hundredth of a yen

explanation.surface: A finance office keeps a Japanese coin in reserve along with a gold piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' looks like a workplace, but the offices is an old British euphemism for the toilet, giving JOHN.
explanation.definitionFit: The johannes, or joe, was a Portuguese gold coin named after King John V, issued in the 18th century.

clue.text: Oval gem bats at event

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so these letters go wild and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: At a cricket ground, the Oval, a jewel of a batting performance at the big event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oval' and 'bats' suggest cricket; 'bats' is the slang word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A navette is a gemstone cut in a pointed oval, boat-shaped outline, also called a marquise.

clue.text: Mysterious idol the principle of beliefs apparently in Thailand

indicators.note: principle here plays on principal, the chief or leading one, so the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word
ap. is a dictionary abbreviation for apparently
someone in is at home
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A strange idol is said to embody the core tenet of Thai religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The principle of beliefs' reads as a doctrine, but it means the principal, leading letter. 'In' gives HOME, as in staying in.
explanation.definitionFit: Baphomet was the idol the Knights Templar were accused of worshipping, a figure of obscure origin later used in occultism.

clue.text: Spiritual fathers retiring drink bolstering the soul

parts.note: in ancient Egyptian belief the ba is the soul

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Holy men going to bed take a drink to fortify the spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the piece that bolsters another sits beneath it, so the drink comes after the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Bapu means father in Hindi and Gujarati, a title of respect for a spiritual leader, famously Gandhi.

clue.text: Alter two notes and copy semitone

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: N is an abbreviation for note, so two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician is told to change two notes and write out a semitone.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical setting makes 'notes' look like pitches; here they are just two abbreviations, N and N.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek music theory a pycnon is a close-packed group of small intervals, used loosely for a semitone.

clue.text: Axes religious ballots lacking hint of efficacy

parts.note: pi is slang for pious

indicators.note: lacking means being without, so that letter is missing
a hint is only a trace, so just the opening letter is meant

parts.note: ballots are votes
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Church ballots that achieve nothing get the axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' looks like the verb meaning cuts; it is the plural of axis.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot is the point or shaft on which something turns, which is what an axis is.

clue.text: Sherry casks are turned over under the sun

indicators.note: in a down answer what lies under comes lower, so that piece is placed second

parts.note: Sol is the sun, from Latin

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Barrels of sherry are rolled over out in the Spanish sun.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer what is 'under' comes below, so the turned word follows the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A solera is the tiered system of casks in which sherry is aged and blended, and the casks themselves.

clue.text: Woman left out breadbasket in chancel of church

indicators.note: out means gone away, so that letter is no longer there

parts.note: a lady is a woman
L abbreviates left
breadbasket is slang for the stomach, the tum

explanation.surface: A woman left a bread basket lying in the chancel of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breadbasket' looks like a real basket, but it is the slang word for the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: An adytum is the innermost sanctuary of a temple, and by extension the chancel, the holiest part of a church.

clue.text: Evergreen clipped like this always coming back

indicators.note: something clipped is trimmed short, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: thus means like this

indicators.note: coming back means returning the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ay is an old word for always, as in for ay

explanation.surface: An evergreen hedge, clipped like this, keeps growing back.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardening picture makes 'clipped' and 'coming back' sound like hedge-trimming; both are signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Thuya, or thuja, is a genus of coniferous trees including arbor vitae, which keep their foliage all year.

clue.text: Navy shelled Iceland with old, old speedy vessel

indicators.note: a shelled nut has its outer case removed, so only the inside letters remain

parts.note: the inner two letters of the word
IS is Iceland's international code, from Island
O abbreviates old

explanation.surface: The navy bombarded Iceland using an old, very old fast ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'old' gives O; the second belongs to the definition, since the vessel is a historical type.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviso was a fast dispatch boat used to carry messages between warships, now a historical craft.

clue.text: Colour stencilling of music ensemble on piano

indicators.note: in an across answer one thing on another follows it, so the last-named piece leads

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
o' is a clipped form of of
a choir is a group of singers

explanation.surface: Coloured stencil designs of a music group are printed on a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on piano' puts the P first. The music words make piano look like the instrument; it is the dynamic marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pochoir is a French technique of hand-colouring prints through a series of stencils, so colour stencilling.

clue.text: Insipid watery stuff, not special

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is excluded

parts.note: blash is a Scots word for a weak watery drink or slop
S abbreviates special

explanation.surface: A bland, watery liquid with nothing special about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Blash is a dictionary word for weak watery food or drink, which the solver may need to look up.
explanation.definitionFit: Blah is an informal adjective for dull or lacking flavour and interest, which is what insipid means.

clue.text: Harmful beetle we eliminated

indicators.note: eliminated means removed, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a weevil is a kind of beetle
taken as written

explanation.surface: We got rid of a destructive beetle pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We eliminated' sounds like pest control; it means the two letters are struck from the front of the beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil as an adjective means causing harm or injury, a direct synonym of harmful.

clue.text: Frenchman possessing singing voice that closely resembles original recording

indicators.note: to possess is to hold, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: René is a common French first name
alto is a singing voice

explanation.surface: A Frenchman whose voice sounds just like his own record.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a single word, a sound clip that matches the original track.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone ringtone made from an actual excerpt of a song, rather than a synthesised imitation, mimics the source closely.

clue.text: Second day holding spade — a way to teach manual skills

definitions.text: a way to teach manual skills

indicators.note: holding means clasping within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: S abbreviates second
a loy is a long narrow Irish spade
D abbreviates day

explanation.surface: On the second day pupils learn to handle a spade, a lesson in practical skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second day' joins S and D, which together hold the spade.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloyd is a Swedish system of education through woodwork and handicraft, training hand and eye.

clue.text: Returning a lot of palm oil

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
a lot of something is most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rattan is a climbing palm

explanation.surface: Bringing back plenty of palm oil from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm oil' looks like one product; palm is the wordplay and oil is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Attar is a fragrant essential oil distilled from flowers, especially rose petals, used in perfume.

clue.text: Performing sea shanties round end of jetty perhaps hearing colours?

indicators.note: a piece being performed is played around with, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end is the final position, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Singers perform sea shanties at the end of a jetty, hearing the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' only says the shanty letters go round the Y before the shuffle. The question mark marks the definition as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Synaesthesia is a crossing of the senses in which, for example, sounds are perceived as colours.
